title: oekaki conventions
description: Where to look in a Terraform repository for facts the language does not standardise. Values are names, not data: which local holds an account id, which variable holds a table of them.

note.description: Why this repository is read the way it is. For the person who finds the file later.

accountFromLocal.description: Locals that hold an AWS account id outright, most trusted first.

accountTable.description: A table of name to account id, and the name a module uses to pick its row.

variable.description: The variable holding the table. The same name is looked for as variable.key or variable["key"] to see which row a module takes.

rootModule.description: What makes a directory one of this estate's own root modules. Without this, any directory holding a backend block is one, which is the right default and the wrong answer for a repository that also keeps examples or vendored copies.

requires.description: File names a directory must contain to count. Any one of them is enough.

stateKeyPrefix.description: A prefix every state key shares, removed from the identifiers so they read as the estate names them rather than as the bucket lays them out.

accountNames.description: Where the names of accounts are written down. Terraform has no idea what an account is called; somewhere in the repository a person did.

file.description: A path, relative to the scanned directory, or a shell-style pattern.

variable.description: A block assigned to this name holds the table. Without it the whole file is read.

pattern.description: A regular expression with two capture groups, name then id, for a file that is not a table. The first group that is not empty is taken as the name.
